Q: Pivoting multiple columns from wide to long A:

I think the two-step code in the OP starts off looking as desired, but it actually goes wrong by pairing every x/y value with every possible style. I'm assuming that the original data was intended to map different functions to different line types, but if we use the code as-is, we'll have every function mapped to every line type, yielding output that is 180 rows long [when the original data only had 20 rows x 3 pairs of data = 60 data points].

df_longer2 |>
  ggplot(aes(x, value, color = y, linetype = style_value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~style_value)

I can't imagine this is what was intended:

@r2evans gives good suggestions for how to wrangle this by translating the column names to underlying meaning by stripping the numbers from them. This produces data that makes more sense to me, where each data point only appears once in the output:

tidyr::pivot_longer(df1, cols = -x, 
                    names_pattern = "(.*)([0-9]+)", 
                    names_to=c(".value","num")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = num, linetype = style)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~style)

Another way we could do this is by making a "manual spec" (see https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/articles/pivot.html#manual-specs). This can offer flexibility in some cases, but is arguably overkill here, since @r2evans' approach does essentially the same thing with less code.

Here, I make a table that contains the column names (except the first, x), and specifies that whatever value is found in that column should be assigned to the column specified in .value, and it assigns values for columns called y_name and style_name, that give those respective column names for each data point.

piv_spec <- tibble(.name = names(df1[,-1])) |>
  mutate(.value = .name |> str_remove("\\d+"),
         col_num = .name |> str_remove("[:alpha:]+"),
         y_name = paste0("y", col_num),
         style_name = paste0("style", col_num))
> piv_spec
# A tibble: 6 × 5
  .name  .value col_num y_name style_name
  <chr>  <chr>  <chr>   <chr>  <chr>     
1 y1     y      1       y1     style1    
2 style1 style  1       y1     style1    
3 y2     y      2       y2     style2    
4 style2 style  2       y2     style2    
5 y3     y      3       y3     style3    
6 style3 style  3       y3     style3

With that, it's very straightforward to reshape:

df1 |>
  pivot_longer_spec(piv_spec)

# A tibble: 60 × 6
       x col_num y_name style_name     y style   
   <int> <chr>   <chr>  <chr>      <dbl> <chr>   
 1     1 1       y1     style1         1 lineA:1 
 2     1 2       y2     style2         1 lineA:2 
 3     1 3       y3     style3         4 points:A
 4     2 1       y1     style1         4 lineA:1 
 5     2 2       y2     style2         8 lineA:2 
 6     2 3       y3     style3         8 points:A
 7     3 1       y1     style1         9 lineA:1 
 8     3 2       y2     style2        27 lineA:2 
 9     3 3       y3     style3        12 points:A
10     4 1       y1     style1        16 lineA:1 
# ℹ 50 more rows

Q: Activate cell working on Chrome on a Windows laptop, but not Android Google Sheets app A:

Google Apps Script methods related to the user interface, like SpreadsheetApp.Range.activate() don't work on Android, however, onEdit simple and installable triggers might work while they don't use UI methods.

The above was not mentioned on the official documentation for years, but it has been updated "silently", so it might be added somewhere. I say "silently" because there are no notifications or a list of changes made to the documentation.

Q: Angular 20 app shows blank page on first load after deploying with --base-href /new/ and Service Worker — works after refresh (only in Production) A:

You have two separate issues that together explain the "blank page on first load, works after refresh" behavior.

(Before trying out the fixes, do the debug test at the bottom to confirm the issue, then proceed with the fixes)

1. You are registering the Service Worker multiple times

You are calling provideServiceWorker('ngsw-worker.js', ...):

  • In main.ts
  • Multiple times inside app.config.ts

Angular must register the Service Worker exactly once. Multiple registrations can cause:

  • Race conditions during install, Corrupted or partial caches etc..

Fix

Keep provideServiceWorker in only one place.

(My Recommendation): keep it in main.ts alone and remove all occurrences from app.config.ts.

Example (only once):

provideServiceWorker('ngsw-worker.js', {
  enabled: !isDevMode(),
  registrationStrategy: 'registerWhenStable:30000'
})

Remove every other provideServiceWorker call.

Additional Info:

  • provideServiceWorker() sets up a root-level APP_INITIALIZER and registers a global browser service worker, so calling it multiple times creates duplicate registrations and race conditions.

  • It should live only in main.ts because that’s the single root bootstrap point, guaranteeing it runs exactly once.

2. Your ngsw-config.json is incorrect for sub-path deployment

You are deploying under:

https://example.com/new/

And building with:

--base-href /new/
--deploy-url /new/

which you did correctly. However, your ngsw-config.json contains:

"index": "/index.html"

When deployed under /new/, the leading slash makes the Service Worker look for in one level up (relative parent directory):

https://example.com/index.html

instead of:

https://example.com/new/index.html

This causes the SW to cache or resolve the wrong index file during first load, resulting in a blank screen.

Fix

Change: Remove the leading slash so it resolves relative to the app root.

"index": "/index.html"

to:

"index": "index.html"

3. Make sure your server rewrite rules are correct

If you are using Angular routing, Hostinger must rewrite all /new/* routes to /new/index.html.

In /new/.htaccess (Apache), you should have something like:

<IfModule mod_rewrite.c>
  RewriteEngine On
  RewriteBase /new/
  RewriteRule ^index\.html$ - [L]
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
  RewriteRule . /new/index.html [L]
</IfModule>

Without this, there are chances initial navigation may fail or behave inconsistently.

First confirm the SW Issue with the steps below

  • First, Temporarily disable the Service Worker:
provideServiceWorker('ngsw-worker.js', { enabled: false })
  • Rebuild and redeploy.
  • Clear all site data in DevTools (Application → Clear storage).
  • Test again.

If the issue disappears completely, it was definitely SW-related.

In short

  • Register the Service Worker only once.
  • Change "index": "/index.html" to "index": "index.html".
  • Ensure proper rewrite rules on Hostinger (opt).
  • After fixing, remove the old Service Worker and clear all site data before retesting.

Q: Find column value within a long string A:

Just flip your logic around and search for your column value in a fixed (or variable) string e.g.

SELECT *   
FROM search_phrase
WHERE 'This is a test for anyone that resides at address 123 Main Street. Please call if you do'
    LIKE '%' + search_string + '%';

Note: You concatenate the wildcards around your column value to ensure it can be found anywhere.

Q: how to get List of GID numbers and List of Sheet Names in Google Sheets? A:

we can do both tasks in multiple ways. here are some examples with requirements and limitations:

first step: share your spreadsheet (if you worry about privacy, just do not share the spreadsheet link with anyone)

LIST OF GID NUMBERS

for gids use:

=VSTACK(, IFERROR(LET(i, A1, INDEX(TOCOL(REGEXEXTRACT(SPLIT(DGET(
 VSTACK(i, IMPORTDATA("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"&i&
 "/preview?gid=0", "|")), i, VSTACK(i, "var gid")), "?gid=", ), 
 """(\d+)"""), 3)*1)), "Loading ..."))

  • recalculation every 60 minutes

  • shows only gids of unhidden sheets

  • sheets are in order of position

  • faster than 1h update needs manual user action via checkbox. recalculation time is fairly reasonable (0-1 min). now the mistery part: the output of IMPORTs is stored temporarily in some unknown shadow cache. this basicaly means that if you add/remove sheet, you may observe the old state for few more seconds, even after hitting that checkbox. however, the effect of the shadow cache can be prolonged even for few minutes, if you have 2 or more such formulae in your spreadsheet. here is the checkboxed fx version:

=VSTACK(, IFERROR(LET(x, A1, 
 y, "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"&x&"/preview?gid=0", 
 INDEX(TOCOL(REGEXEXTRACT(SPLIT(DGET(VSTACK(x, 
 IF(A2, IMPORTDATA(y, "|"), IMPORTXML(y, "//script"))), 
 x, VSTACK(x, "*var gid")), "?gid=", ), """(\d+)"""), 3)*1)), "Loading ..."))

and from here you can easily make a jumping links like:

=INDEX(IF(A5:A="",, HYPERLINK("#gid="&A5:A&"&range=C5", "jump to C5")))

these formulae can be modded to extract sheet names instead of gids, but you would get those sheet names with JS-style hex escape sequence in it if you would use exotic sheet names. to fix them you would need to run CHAR(HEX2DEC( functions:

LIST OF SHEET NAMES

for sheets try:

=VSTACK(, IF(A2, INDEX(LET(i, A1, x, CHAR(65535),
 y, IMPORTHTML("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"&i&"/view?gid=0", "table", 2), 
 z, IFERROR(INDEX(y, 2, 3), "LOADING ..."), 
 TOCOL(SUBSTITUTE(SPLIT(REGEXREPLACE(z, "(\n)'","$1"&x), CHAR(10)), x, CHAR(39)), 2)))))

  • recalculation every 60 minutes

  • shows sheet names of all sheets

  • show sheet names of hidden sheets

  • sheet names without JS-style hex escape sequence

  • sheets are in order of position

  • works with exotic sheet names

  • supports 99.99% of printable unicode characters

  • faster than 1h update needs manual user action via checkbox. recalculation time is fairly reasonable (0-2 min). also the mistery part: the output of IMPORT is stored temporarily in some unknown shadow cache. this basicaly means that if you add/remove/rename sheet, you may observe the old state for few more seconds, even after switching that checkbox. however, the effect of the shadow cache can be prolonged even for few minutes, if you have 2 or more such formulae in your spreadsheet. if it gets stuborn smash that checkbox few more times.

and again, active references easily done with BYROW like:

=BYROW(A5:A, LAMBDA(x, IF(x="",,IFERROR(INDIRECT(x&"!D1")))))

  • a new way how to stop freeze recalculating random numbers

  • an alternative way how to get individual updateable sheet names

  • a guide to redo any formula to different semicolon ; syntax type

  • a way of constructing infinite truly dynamic ranges and QUERY smashing

Q: How to check if a column value is in a string SQL A: 
SELECT * from TABLE where LOCATE(COLUMN, @STRING)>0;

LOCATE(a,b) returns a number giving the character location of a in b, or returns 0.

See Mysql LOCATE()

The docs discuss that LOCATE() is only case sensitive when one of the strings is a 'binary string'. That probably doesn't affect your use case, though if it became an issue you could CONVERT() the binary strings to a locale and use LOWER() to get lower case.
